p: We find joy mentioned in the Torah
and "on the day of your rejoicing" (Bamidbar 10:10),
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
And this follows what they said in the Midrash
נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בָּךְ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ד) —
"'We will exult and rejoice in You' (Shir HaShirim 1:4):
'This is the day that Hashem has made,
let us exult and rejoice in it' (Tehillim 118:24) —
we do not know in what to rejoice,
אִם בַּיּוֹם אִם בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא;
whether in the day or in Hakadosh Baruch Hu.
'We will exult and rejoice in You' —
'in You' — in Your salvation; 'in You' — in Your Torah;
which is salvation from all evil,
that we merit to make the heart upright,
emptying out all evil from the heart of the fool.
And the upright are destined for joy,
"and for the upright of heart, joy"
corresponds to Shavuos, the time of the giving of the Torah,
"The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart."
דְּאִיתָא (תַּעֲנִית ח, ב וּפֵרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י שָׁם)
as is brought (Taanis 8b and Rashi there):
"Those who fear My Name" — those who keep Shabbos.
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the unlearned."
וְאִיתָא (תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג):
And it is brought (Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, beginning of ch. 3):
"My joy is out of my fear."
And this is what we say,
"They shall rejoice in Your kingship," etc.:
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?";
"a king, whose awe shall be upon you."
"and you shall rejoice before Hashem your God
"And you shall rejoice in your festival," etc.,
For Sukkos includes all three joys.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, ב)
according to what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 30:2):
"Whoever takes the palm branches in his hand,
we know that they are the victors," etc.;
"with their lulavim and esrogim in their hands,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קג, א):
according to what they said (Zohar III 103a):
under the shade of faith," etc.;
"and whoever is within the mystery of faith
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, Hakadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds —
immediately fear comes to him, etc.
and "my joy is out of my fear."
נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ,
corresponds to what it says, "and you shall be only joyful,"
for Shemini Atzeres is the wellsprings of the Torah;
and in Eretz Yisrael we complete the Torah on it,
and we circle with the Sefer Torah,
so that there be an encompassing light
in the language of the Sages, simply "the Chag";
מִלְּשׁוֹן יָחוֹגּוּ וְיָנוּעוּ כַּשִּׁכּוֹר (תְּהִלִּים קז, כז),
from the expression "they reel and stagger like a drunkard" (Tehillim 107:27) —
And on Sukkos we circle the Sefer Torah
as they used to circle the Altar in the Mikdash.
"Yaakov is at the head of the rejoicing," etc.
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, ב),
the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for the Name Havayah,
as explained in the holy Zohar:
"The Torah is the Name of Hakadosh Baruch Hu"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם צח, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב,
(as written there, 98, end of side b,
and we rejoice and circle with the Torah.
and this is what we say (piyut for Simchas Torah),
כִּי חַיִּים הוּא לָנוּ עוֹז וְאוֹרָה —
"For it is life for us, strength and light" —
for the Torah is called life,
"See, I have set before you life."
"Strength" corresponds to "in You — in Your salvation,"
"Fortunate is the man whose strength is in You";
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רסט, סוֹף עַמּוּד א);
(as written in Zohar III, end of 269a);
"Hashem will give strength to His people,"
וְנִדְרָשׁ עַל מַתַּן תּוֹרָה (זְבָחִים קטז, א).
which is expounded as referring to Matan Torah (Zevachim 116a).
And salvation is chiefly from the yetzer hara,
which is the hater and the enemy,
(בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וַיֵּרָא, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נד, א)
(in the Midrash Rabbah on Vayeira, Bereishis Rabbah 54:1):
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז) —
"'Even his enemies He makes at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7) —
that breaks the yetzer hara except Torah"
And "light" is "in You — in Your fear,"
for the essential light that should shine before him
is that the King of kings
stands over him and sees his deeds;
"like the fear of flesh and blood";
meaning that there is a fear greater than this:
stands over him and sees his deeds.
And this is the essential light:
"and illuminate our eyes in Your Torah."
And this is what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4):
"'Hashem is my light' — on Rosh Hashanah."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
And this is along the lines of what Tikkunei Zohar says
And then there is fear and dread
And this is "in You — in Your fear,"
and "my joy is out of my fear":
